evals.prompt: I'm planning the first-ever gala for Desert Bloom Refugee Services in Phoenix — target date April 25, ~250 guests at a hotel ballroom. The hotel quoted $95/person for food and bev plus a $4,000 room fee. We want to net $120,000. We're thinking live auction, silent auction and some kind of paddle raise. Can you build the budget with ticket pricing and a revenue plan?
evals.expected_output: A budget with conservative, target and stretch scenarios across every revenue stream and a full expense list including staff time, platform fees, insurance and a 5-10% contingency. It shows net alongside gross and cost to raise a dollar, prices tickets cost-plus-philanthropy with the deductible portion stated, and sets a fixed-cost floor so fund-a-need is not the make-or-break line.
assertions: Starts from the $120,000 net goal and works backward to the required revenue mix, presenting net revenue alongside gross
Models conservative, target and stretch scenarios for each revenue stream (tickets, sponsorships, live auction, silent auction, fund-a-need)
The expense budget includes auction platform fees, insurance, staff time and a contingency line of about 5-10%

Prices tickets cost-plus-philanthropy (covering the ~$95 per-plate cost plus a premium) and notes receipts must state the deductible portion above fair market value, to be checked against IRS Publication 1771
Identifies a ticket and sponsorship floor that covers fixed costs at conservative attendance so the paddle raise isn't relied on to avoid a loss
Calculates cost to raise a dollar (expense / revenue) and treats any external benchmark as a rough reference only

evals.prompt: Gala is in 3 weeks. Need the run of show. Doors at 6, dinner, a client speaker, live auction with 14 lots, fund-a-need for our new teen center, silent auction closes at some point. We have 20 volunteers. — Mia, Westfield Boys & Girls Club
evals.expected_output: A minute-by-minute run of show with named owners and scripted transitions. The beneficiary story comes right before the tiered fund-a-need, the live auction is trimmed from 14 lots, and the staffing plan prioritizes checkout.
assertions: Provides a timed run of show (doors, cocktail and silent auction window, seating, program, speaker, live auction, fund-a-need, silent close and checkout, end) with a named owner or role for each segment
Recommends cutting the live auction from 14 lots toward about 5-10, citing bidder fatigue
Places the client speaker or beneficiary story right before the fund-a-need ask and structures the ask in tiered giving levels
The volunteer plan covers check-in, auction runners, VIP hosting and especially checkout/payment, flagged as the most common day-of bottleneck
Notes every auction item needs a documented fair market value on its bid sheet

evals.prompt: Our board wants to add a 50/50 raffle and a 'wine pull' game to our gala at Hope House (we're in Texas), and the board chair also wants to tell the board we 'raised $310,000' last year. Expenses were about $175,000 including the hotel and auction platform but not counting staff time. Thoughts on both?
evals.expected_output: The response tells the user to check raffle and game-of-chance legality with the state regulator before adding them. It also argues for reporting net revenue (and cost to raise a dollar including staff time) instead of the $310K gross.
assertions: Says raffles and games of chance are state-regulated and must be checked against current rules from the state regulator (attorney general or gaming commission) for Texas before being added, without asserting what Texas law permits
Advises reporting net revenue alongside gross: $310K gross minus about $175K expense nets about $135K, and that is before staff time
Notes staff time is often left out of event expenses, which overstates profit, and recommends including it in cost to raise a dollar
Calculates or recommends cost to raise a dollar (expense / revenue) as the efficiency metric

should_not_trigger.query: Design Presenting, Gold and Silver sponsorship packages for our gala and price them.
Plan our 5K charity run where participants recruit friends to sponsor them — team captain toolkit and fundraising page goals.
